# Skeleton: `jl-skeleton`

A shimmering placeholder in the shape of content that is loading.

- Class `JlSkeleton`, an atom: `import { JlSkeleton } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/skeleton

Skeletons hold the place of content that is loading, in its shape, so the page does not jump when it
arrives. Use them for loads that take more than a moment; for short waits, a spinner on the button is enough.

Screen readers skip skeletons: set aria-busy="true" on the region they fill, and remove it once the content is in.
With reduced motion, the shimmer stops.

## Use

```ts
import { JlSkeleton } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlSkeleton lines={3} shape="text" />
```

```html
<jl-skeleton lines="3" shape="text"></jl-skeleton>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `shape` (attribute `shape`): `'text' | 'rect' | 'circle'`, default `'text'`. Lines of text, a block, or a circle.
- `width` (attribute `width`): `string`, default `''`. A CSS length (a plain number is in pixels). Text and blocks fill the width; a circle is 40px.
- `height` (attribute `height`): `string`, default `''`. A CSS length. Text lines follow the font size, blocks are 96px, a circle matches its width.
- `lines` (attribute `lines`): `number`, default `1`. For text: how many lines.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The box around the lines or the shape.
- `--base` (custom property): The placeholder colour.
- `--shine` (custom property): The colour of the shimmer that crosses it.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### Text

Lines of text; the last of several is shorter.

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <jl-skeleton></jl-skeleton>
  <jl-skeleton lines="3"></jl-skeleton>
</div>
```

### Circles and blocks

Sizes take any CSS length; a plain number is in pixels.

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-skeleton shape="circle" width="24"></jl-skeleton>
  <jl-skeleton shape="circle"></jl-skeleton>
  <jl-skeleton shape="circle" width="56"></jl-skeleton>
  <jl-skeleton shape="rect" width="160" height="90"></jl-skeleton>
  <jl-skeleton shape="rect" width="90" height="90"></jl-skeleton>
</div>
```

### A list loading

The shape of a list of people while it loads.

```html
<div class="stack narrow" aria-busy="true">
  <div class="row">
    <jl-skeleton shape="circle"></jl-skeleton>
    <div class="stack" style="flex: 1; gap: 8px">
      <jl-skeleton width="40%"></jl-skeleton>
      <jl-skeleton width="70%"></jl-skeleton>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="row">
    <jl-skeleton shape="circle"></jl-skeleton>
    <div class="stack" style="flex: 1; gap: 8px">
      <jl-skeleton width="55%"></jl-skeleton>
      <jl-skeleton width="80%"></jl-skeleton>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### A card loading

In a card: a picture, a heading and a paragraph.

```html
<jl-card class="narrow" aria-busy="true">
  <jl-skeleton slot="media" shape="rect" height="120" style="--jl-radius: 0"></jl-skeleton>
  <div class="stack">
    <jl-skeleton width="50%" style="font-size: 20px"></jl-skeleton>
    <jl-skeleton lines="3"></jl-skeleton>
  </div>
</jl-card>
```
